local_market_longform:
New Orleans is its own market, and a cash sale here works differently than the national talking points suggest. Homes in New Orleans currently trade around a median of $310,000 and take roughly 52 days to go under contract, with about 26% of area sales closing in cash. When you need certainty instead of a drawn-out listing — a firm number and a date you choose — that local pace is exactly why selling directly makes sense.

The housing stock shapes everything about condition here. New Orleans runs heavily to 1800s–1920s shotguns, doubles, and Creole cottages, plus post-war ranches in Gentilly and the east, and each era carries its own repair realities. That matters because we price the house in front of us rather than asking you to renovate it first — the things a traditional buyer's inspector flags are the same things we already expect and account for.

Local conditions are the other factor a generic buyer ignores. Around New Orleans, the issues we see most are hurricane and flood risk below sea level, subsidence and settling of pier foundations, termite and moisture rot, and post-storm roof and water damage. We've made offers on homes with every one of those problems, so none of it scares us off or kills the deal at the last minute.

We buy across the whole area — from close-in neighborhoods like the Ninth Ward out to Metairie and Kenner — and in Louisiana the local economy anchored by the port, tourism and hospitality, energy, and healthcare keeps demand real. Inherited homes, tired rentals, pre-foreclosure situations in Orleans Parish, and houses that simply need more work than the owner wants to take on: those are the New Orleans sellers we help most.

Being a genuinely local buyer near the French Quarter also means our offer isn't a lowball pulled from a national algorithm that has never seen New Orleans. We know what a block in the Ninth Ward, Gentilly, Mid-City, and Algiers actually sells for, what southeast Louisiana buyers will and won't pay for, and how Orleans Parish's title and closing process really works. That local read is why our sellers get a number they can trust and a closing that actually happens on the date we promised.

faq.q: How fast can you close on my New Orleans house?
faq.a: As little as 7 days through a licensed Louisiana title company, or any later date you choose. Sellers in New Orleans pick the timeline that fits their move.

faq.q: Do I pay any fees or commissions?
faq.a: None. No agent commissions, no listing fees, and we cover standard closing costs. The number we agree on is what you receive.

faq.q: Do I need to repair or clean the house first?
faq.a: No. We buy New Orleans homes in any condition — including the hurricane and flood risk below sea level we see so often here. Take what you want and leave the rest.

faq.q: How do you decide the offer amount?
faq.a: We look at recent comparable sales in your New Orleans neighborhood — places like the Ninth Ward — the home's condition, and current southeast Louisiana demand, then make a fair cash offer you're free to accept or decline.

faq.q: Is this a licensed, legitimate way to sell in Louisiana?
faq.a: Yes. We are a direct buyer, not your agent or broker, and we put that in writing. Louisiana has no wholesaling-specific statute; we buy directly and disclose our interest in writing.

faq.q: Can you help with foreclosure, probate, or tenants?
faq.a: Often, yes. We regularly work with Orleans Parish sellers facing foreclosure, probate, liens, or tenant issues, and we structure the sale around the situation.
